questions.q: What is an external location, as its own governed object?
options: A folder inside DBFS root with no governance at all
A type of cluster used only for external data sources
A synonym for a catalog's MANAGED LOCATION
A specific cloud path bound to a storage credential, with its own GRANT/REVOKE permissions
questions.explain: An external location binds a cloud path to a credential and is itself a securable object, granted and revoked exactly like a table.

questions.q: What does a storage credential actually wrap?
options: The schema of every table in a catalog
A user's personal Databricks login password
A cached copy of table data for faster reads
A real cloud identity, such as a managed identity or service principal
questions.explain: A storage credential wraps a real cloud identity so Unity Catalog can authenticate to storage without exposing keys to users.

questions.q: Why do users get GRANTs on the external location instead of the storage credential?
options: Because catalogs no longer support any form of permission
The credential is infrastructure — users should never see or touch access keys directly
Storage credentials cannot be granted to anyone under any circumstances
External locations and storage credentials are actually the same object
questions.explain: Credentials are infrastructure; day-to-day permissions belong on the external location, keeping keys out of users' hands entirely.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what did Databricks & Delta Lake Lessons 39-40 already cover in full?
options: The catalog.schema.table namespace and a catalog's own MANAGED LOCATION
Auto Loader's file notification mode
Row-level and column-level security
External locations and storage credentials
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly recaps that material rather than re-teaching it, then covers what those lessons left out.

questions.q: Can an external table or external volume point at any cloud path, with no other setup?
options: No — the path must already have an external location registered over it
Only for tables, never for volumes
Only if the path is inside the catalog's own managed location
Yes — external tables can point at any unregistered path freely
questions.explain: Unity Catalog requires the path to sit under a registered external location before an external table or volume can reference it.
